definition: Hospitalization is receiving care in a hospital. In this mental health context, it refers to a level of service some youths may sometimes need as part of their treatment.

reasons: The packet supports only that some youth with DMDD may sometimes require hospitalization as part of mental health care; it does not define hospitalization as “receiving care in a hospital.”
The added gloss about “a level of service some youths may sometimes need as part of their treatment” goes beyond the packet’s wording and is broader than the source evidence provided.

The definition claims hospitalization is “a level of service some youths may sometimes need,” but the packet only states that youths “sometimes” need “mental health care services, including doctor visits and sometimes hospitalization” and does not describe a “level of service” concept.

The definition labels the statement as “In this mental health context, it refers to a level of service… as part of their treatment,” but the packet does not explicitly frame hospitalization as a “level of service” or explicitly tie it to “their treatment” beyond listing it among care services.
The definition’s field is set to “cognition,” but neither the packet nor the definition indicates a cognition-specific meaning (e.g., attention, memory, thinking processes).
